en: Dhātukathā 2:
Niddesa 2.12.
Exposition of the Twelve Methods Concerning the Included and Unincluded Among the Associated [States] (Sampayutta-saṅgahita-asaṅgahita-pada-niddesa)
Those phenomena associated with the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha),
those phenomena associated with the aggregate of perception (saññākkhandha),

and those phenomena associated with the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)— by how many aggregates, by how many bases (āyatana), and by how many elements (dhātu) are these phenomena comprised?
Those phenomena are included within three aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena associated with the aggregate of consciousness;
those phenomena associated with the mind-base;
those phenomena associated with the eye-consciousness element; and so forth...

Those phenomena associated with the mind-element (manodhātu) … those phenomena associated with the mind-consciousness-element (manoviññāṇadhātu) … these phenomena are comprised within three aggregates (khandha), one base (āyatana), and one element (dhātu).
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Those phenomena which [are not included] by the truth of the origin...
Those phenomena associated with the truth of the path are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena associated with the mind-faculty are included in three aggregates, one base, and one element.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
By the faculty of pleasure, those phenomena which...
Those phenomena associated with the faculty of pain … those phenomena associated with the faculty of mental joy … those phenomena associated with the faculty of mental grief …
Those phenomena are included within three aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those states associated with the faculty of equanimity are included within three aggregates, two bases, and seven elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, ten bases, and eleven elements.
Those phenomena which [are associated] with the faculty of faith...
those phenomena which [are associated] with the faculty of energy...
Those phenomena by means of the faculty of mindfulness … those phenomena by means of the faculty of concentration … those phenomena by means of the faculty of wisdom …
The phenomena associated with the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," the phenomena associated with the faculty of higher knowledge,
and the phenomena associated with the faculty of one who has already known.
Those phenomena which are associated with ignorance...
those phenomena which are associated with the volitional formations conditioned by ignorance...
those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena associated with consciousness conditioned by volitional formations (saṅkhāra-paccaya-viññāṇa) …
Those phenomena are included within three aggregates, one base, and one element.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Those phenomena associated with contact conditioned by the six sense bases:
those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena associated with feeling conditioned by contact are included in three aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena [arising] from feeling as condition for craving...
Those states that are associated with clinging conditioned by craving,
and those states that are associated with kamma-existence—
these states are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).
As for the states [associated] with sorrow...
Those phenomena that are associated with suffering … those phenomena that are associated with mental grief … those phenomena are comprised within three aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena which [are associated] with despair...
Those phenomena associated with the foundations of mindfulness,
those phenomena associated with the right efforts, and so forth—
those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).
As for those phenomena associated with the basis of psychic power (iddhipāda) …
Those phenomena are included within three aggregates, one base, and one element.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Those states that are associated with jhāna are comprised by three aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not comprised?
They are not included within two aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena that belong to the immeasurables… those phenomena that belong to the five faculties…
Those states that are associated with the five powers… those states that are associated with the seven factors of enlightenment… those states that are associated with the noble eightfold path…
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena associated with contact...
those phenomena associated with volition...
those phenomena associated with attention...
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena associated with feeling...
those phenomena associated with perception...
those phenomena are comprised within three aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by two aggregates, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena which are associated with the mind...
Those phenomena are included within three aggregates, one base, and one element.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Those phenomena associated with resolve (adhimokkha) ...
those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements.
2.12.1. Triplet:
Those phenomena which are associated with states that are associated with pleasant feeling...

Those phenomena that [arise] with states associated with painful feeling … those phenomena that [arise] with states associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling … those phenomena that [arise] with states accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought …
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena that are without applied thought but have sustained thought;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by rapture;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by pleasure.
Those states which are associated with states accompanied by equanimity are included in one aggregate, in one base, and in one element.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
The Group on Roots (Hetu-gocchaka)

Those phenomena which [are associated] with root-phenomena … those phenomena which [are associated] with both root-phenomena and phenomena accompanied by roots … those phenomena which are associated with both root-phenomena and phenomena associated with roots …
Those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that have causes but are not themselves causes;
those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that are associated with causes but are not themselves causes;
those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that are neither causes nor have causes.
Those states are included in one aggregate, in one base, and in one element.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included in four aggregates, in eleven bases, and in seventeen elements.
2.12.2.3. Chapter on the Taints (Āsavagocchaka).
Those phenomena which [arise] from the taints;
those phenomena which [arise] from both the taints and the phenomena associated with the taints.
Those states which are associated with both the taints (āsava) and the states associated with the taints...
those states are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena associated with phenomena that are associated with the taints but are themselves not taints are included in one aggregate, one base, and one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
2.12.2.4–9. The Group on Fetters (Saṃyojana-gocchaka), etc.
Those phenomena which [are associated] with the phenomena of the fetters;
those phenomena which [are associated] with the phenomena of the ties;
those phenomena which [are associated] with the phenomena of the floods.
Those phenomena which [are opposed] to the phenomena of the yokes...
those phenomena which [are opposed] to the phenomena of the hindrances...
those phenomena which [are opposed] to the phenomena of the perversions...
Those phenomena which are associated with both the perversions (*parāmāsa*) and the objects pervaded by them (*parāmaṭṭha*) ...
those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates (*khandha*), two bases (*āyatana*), and two elements (*dhātu*).
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena associated with the phenomena associated with the perversions are included in one aggregate, one base, and one element.
By how many is it not included?
It is not included by four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
2.12.2.10. The Great Intermediate Dyads.
Those phenomena which are associated with the mental phenomena (citta-dhamma) … those phenomena are included within three aggregates, one base, and one element.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within two aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Those phenomena which are mental factors;
those phenomena which are associated with consciousness...
Those phenomena [conditioned] by phenomena associated with mind;
those phenomena [conditioned] by phenomena associated with and originated by mind;
those phenomena [conditioned] by phenomena associated with, originated by, and co-existent with mind.
Those states which are associated with states that are conjoined with, originated by, and follow upon the mind:
those states are included within one aggregate, one base, and seven elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
2.12.2.11–13. The Group on Grasping, etc.:
Those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena that are objects of grasping...
Those phenomena which [arise] with defiled phenomena;
those phenomena which [arise] with both defiled and defiling phenomena;
those phenomena which [arise] with both defiled and defiled phenomena.
Those states which are associated with both the defilements and the states associated with the defilements… those states are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena which are associated with defiled phenomena but are not themselves defilements;
those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that are conjoined with defilements but are not themselves defilements...
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by applied thought;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by sustained thought;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by rapture.

By how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are those states comprised which are associated with states accompanied by rapture, those states which are associated with states accompanied by pleasure, and those states which are associated with states accompanied by equanimity?
Those states are included in one aggregate (khandha), in one base (āyatana), and in one element (dhātu).
In how many are they not included?
They are not included in four aggregates, in eleven bases, and in seventeen elements.
The four formless aggregates,
the mind base itself,
and the seven consciousness elements.
Two truths, fourteen faculties;
twelve terms for conditions,
and sixteen thereafter.
In the *Tika* [section], there are eight groups;
in the *Mahantaraduka*, exactly forty-three;
and seven in the *Mahantaraduka*.
There are six in the "Back of the Duka" section;
these have been included in the exposition of the ninth section. [120]
The twelfth section: The Exposition of the Terms "Included by Association" and "Not Included by Association."
